source.title: An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training
source.authors: Sam McCandlish; J. Kaplan; D. Amodei; OpenAI Dota Team

record.file_problem: The full text is present; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares batch-size scaling using test-loss goals, a different measure from the fixed-epoch held-out performance in V5.
record.gate_note: The main batch-size experiments use training performance. Appendix E.3 reports test-loss scaling but does not report held-out error at fixed epoch budgets.
record.test_reason: The study measures optimization efficiency and critical batch size, including efficiency toward test-loss goals. These results do not establish V5's held-out performance difference at fixed epoch budgets. References to a generalization penalty and its removal by tuning describe prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Appendix E.3 but omits the main conclusion: gradient noise scale approximately predicts the critical batch size across diverse tasks, and a roughly hyperbolic relationship describes the tradeoff between optimization steps and examples processed. The late dip in test-based critical batch size is preliminary and left for further investigation.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates batch-size scaling and critical batch size; its test-set analysis uses test-loss goals rather than fixed-epoch held-out performance comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-loss difference appears at the very end of training; early train and test results show no difference.

fits_no_version.finding: For small image-classification datasets, test-based critical batch size resembles training-based results early in training and dips slightly at the end.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The batch size characterizing optimization efficiency toward test-loss goals can decrease slightly late in training relative to training-based scaling.

record.problems: The test-loss analysis is described as preliminary; the text gives no numerical size or uncertainty for the dip, and the reported result is in a figure as well as a qualitative description.
record.rows_left_out: No additional test-loss rows are stated separately in the text; Figure 19 is described only as results for the small image classification datasets in aggregate.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting paired with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Held-out comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Held-out performance across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets, and whether recipe adaptations remove that penalty.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against other measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Training-based batch-scaling results, model-size effects on noise scale, and adaptive-batch efficiency gains do not directly test the supplied claim versions. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Held-out performance comparisons across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets, and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on test error.
Sharpness or other trained-network properties tracking the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: small image classification datasets (aggregate; individual models not specified for this result)
rows.operation_detail: Compared critical batch size when optimizing test-loss goals with training-loss results.
rows.measure: Critical batch size (Bcrit) inferred from batch-size scaling toward test-loss goals.
rows.baseline: training-loss results; no difference early in training
rows.value: a small dip in Bcrit for the test loss, consistently across datasets, at the very end of training
rows.note: This reports test-loss scaling, not held-out error at a fixed epoch budget, so it cannot establish the V5 outcome.
rows.check: The qualitative dip is accurately recorded, but critical batch size is not the fixed-epoch held-out performance effect in V5. The subjects can be identified: CNNs on MNIST and SVHN, and ResNet-32 on CIFAR-10 (Sections 3.2 and A.4.1). The supplied figure text does not provide numerical dip sizes or separate results by optimizer.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
